Subject: Consolidated billing & VAT handling — NovaFields

Hi Soojin,

We're getting our accounting team set up to receive consolidated monthly invoices from Redwood for all NovaFields entities in the EU. A few items we need to confirm before we can move forward:

1) Reverse-charge treatment: we need a clear statement on the invoice that reverse-charge applies (B2B services) and the supplier VAT field left blank where applicable.
2) VAT ID validation: can Redwood provide an automated validation check (VIES) and a PDF/evidence return so we can keep our audit trail?
3) Marketplace / reseller flows: some of our purchases are routed via local resellers — can Redwood support self-billing for those transactions or will we need a separate invoice per reseller?
4) Invoice timing: we'd like a single consolidated invoice by the 5th business day of the month covering prior month usage; payment terms will be net 30.

I've attached our company VAT certificate for your records. Please loop in billing and tax ops and let me know next steps and any forms we need to sign.

Thanks,
Karen Martin
Head of Finance — NovaFields Inc.

Hi Karen — thanks for the clear summary and the VAT certificate. 

Short answers up front: yes, we can issue a consolidated monthly invoice with reverse-charge wording for B2B EU customers; we run an automated VIES check and can include the validation result and timestamp as a PDF attachment at month-end; and we support a self-billing agreement for reseller flows but need a signed template in place.

Action items from our side:
- Ben (billing) will confirm the invoice layout and the exact phrasing we use for reverse-charge (we normally include both the supplier VAT field blank and a line that reads: "Reverse charge — customer liable for VAT under Article 44/196").
- Laura (tax ops) will confirm whether reseller line items must be split on the invoice or can be consolidated under a self-bill.
- I'll send our self-bill template (attached) and a DocuSign link for signature.

Can you confirm the legal entity and VAT number you want on file (the certificate shows two registrations)? Also confirm whether the majority of spend is directly billed or via resellers so we can suggest the simplest consolidation approach.

I'll follow up with the DocuSign link and a sample invoice (PDF) showing the reverse-charge wording.

Best,

Hi Karen — quick note from billing.

Two practical items we need confirmed before enabling consolidated monthly self-billing:
- Required invoice line fields: account name (legal entity), VAT number, tax point (service date), gross amount per line, reverse-charge indicator per line for EU B2B items, and a subtotal for market-place/reseller-sourced charges.
- Reseller handling: if the supplier of record is the reseller (they invoice you), we cannot (and should not) backfill reverse-charge on our invoice. For marketplace flows where Redwood is the supplier of record but collects via resellers, we can include a single invoice with a per-line flag indicating "self-billed via reseller" — but that requires the signed self-bill agreement and reseller attestation.

One procedural note: our VAT ID validation will call VIES and flag any non-matches for manual review. If the VAT ID fails validation for a given month and the customer wants reverse-charge, we may need a corrective workflow (invoice reissue) — please confirm the acceptable tolerance for that (same month reissue vs. next month).

If you can confirm the primary legal entity and whether you expect >85% of spend to be directly billed to that entity versus resellers, we can draft the first consolidated sample for Jan usage.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Billing Operations — Redwood Inference
